passage:
There was an old bowl in Mia's kitchen. It had a crack on one side, so no one used it for soup anymore.
Mia's mother filled it with soil and planted green onions inside. The bowl sat by the window, and new leaves grew from it.
Mia asked why they did not just throw it away.
Her mother said, "It cannot do its old job, but it can still do a new one."
Weeks later, Mia cut green onions from the bowl for dinner. She looked at the crack and thought it made the bowl more interesting.
The old bowl taught her that broken things are not always finished. Sometimes they only need a different purpose.
